rationale.why: Fat provider interfaces force read-only patterns to depend on write APIs they never use, bloat mocks in tests, prevent SSR optimization (read can be server, write must be client), and violate Interface Segregation. Capability-based providers expose granular tokens (`products:read`, `products:write`, `products:stream`) that patterns can request independently.

composition-rules.rule: Providers compose via reduceRight to avoid O(N²) re-renders.
Capability composition is order-independent within a provider; cross-provider order is declared at app level.
Patterns receive capabilities through `ctx[token]`, NOT through useContext directly.
Missing required capability → pattern skipped + warn() in dev.
SSR: capabilities with runtime:'server' resolved server-side; runtime:'client' deferred to hydration.

gates.gate: Provider exposes each capability with its own factory.
Read capability NEVER returns write methods.
Provider has a *.contract.test.ts validating each capability returns the expected shape.
Provider declares runtime hint for SSR optimization.
Provider with signals=true uses signal primitives, not React state, for high-frequency updates.
